# Old Wisdom // Retold
Old Wisdom // Retold is a teen-growth platform for ages 12–17. Its teen-facing Playbooks turn durable ideas from strategy, philosophy, and human psychology into short, practical chapters for real-life situations such as group chats, awkward conversations, friendship shifts, conflict, and follow-through. Its separate Parent Growth layer helps adults SEE → UNDERSTAND → REFLECT → GUIDE → RELEASE so teens build judgment, capability, ownership, and independence. The Playbooks remain entirely teen-facing; parent education lives only in the Parent Hub. Author: Eric Han, Auckland NZ. No dating content, no swearing, and 5–8-minute chapters built for reluctant readers.

## Books
- Book 1: The Social Playbook - friendship, fake friends, group-chat drama, influence (Carnegie, Socrates). https://a.co/d/0gjqlkB6
- Book 2: The War Playbook - bullies, rivalries, pile-ons, composure under pressure (Sun Tzu's Art of War, zero violence glorification). https://a.co/d/0gu0a2CR
- Book 3: The Discipline Playbook - coming (the Stoics)

## Pages
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/: canonical teen-growth platform homepage with The Social Playbook and The War Playbook, Parent Hub guidance, a free sample chapter, and routes to the free skills reflection
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/quiz.html: free 15-question social skills reflection (teen and parent versions)

## Parent Hub
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/parents/: Parent Growth guides organised by SEE → UNDERSTAND → REFLECT → GUIDE → RELEASE.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/quiet-kids-and-confidence: Give a quiet teenager room to answer without turning a pause into a label.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/help-teen-start-conversation-without-making-it-weird: A calmer way to coach the first social move without pushing a quiet teenager to perform.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/signs-of-real-teen-confidence: Notice growing confidence through choices, voice, boundaries, brave action, and recovery without adding pressure.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/why-teen-friendships-fade-after-one-term: Help a teenager understand friendship drift and choose one small follow-up without taking over the relationship.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/quiet-or-lonely-teen: Use context, change, and cost to distinguish restorative time alone from unwanted disconnection without treating quietness as a problem.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/pushing-shy-teen-socialize: Interrupt the Social Pressure Loop and help a shy or socially reluctant teenager take a manageable step without making honest disclosure feel costly.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/more-friends-better-friendship-judgment: Help your teenager look beyond friend count, notice reciprocity, pressure, boundaries, and repair, and choose one safe next move while you keep the safety line.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/before-call-it-disrespect: Use BEFORE → BEHAVIOUR → REPAIR to separate context from permission, keep a clear boundary, and help your teenager return to what they still owe.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/helpful-advice-sounds-like-criticism: A simple three-step check to help parents give useful advice without turning it into another lecture.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/argument-stop-or-communication-improve: A bounded three-step practice for helping teenagers state a view, hear a real limit, and carry the next responsibility after escalation ends.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/why-is-my-teen-avoiding-me: A practical parent guide to reading sudden teen distance without diagnosing it, respecting touch and public-contact boundaries, repairing relational hurts, and keeping a low-pressure route back to connection.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/screenshot-test-angry-message: A quick parent-and-teen check for turning one angry draft into a clearer choice before it leaves the phone.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/read-teen-behaviour-without-guessing: A plain-language guide to separating visible teen behaviour from assumptions, checking the pattern, asking one useful question, and choosing connection, coaching, a boundary, or qualified help.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/teen-friend-always-in-crisis: Help a caring teenager distinguish ordinary support from dangerous secrets, bring capable adults into serious risk, and set humane limits without taking over the friendship.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/teen-driving-curfew-trust-ladder: Separate the driving cut-off from the home time, set a lawful safety floor, and give a newly licensed teen a visible path toward more driving freedom.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/leave-group-drama-safely: Help your teen sort ordinary disagreement from group drama and danger, choose repair or exit, set a neutral boundary, secure accounts, escalate responsibly, and recover.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/teen-left-out-by-friends: Help your teen name the hurt, separate facts from the story, choose one proportionate next move and widen the week without attacking other teenagers or taking over ordinary friendship decisions.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/stand-up-without-fighting: Help your teen use one firm line, move toward safety, report observable facts to a named adult, and follow up without turning dignity into a fight for the crowd.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/teen-wont-talk-after-school: A low-pressure arrival routine that helps parents give a quiet teen room to reset, notice meaningful changes, ask one smaller question, and return without turning concern into a chase.
- https://oldwisdomretold.com/articles/quiet-teen-team-sport-belonging: Help your quiet teen access team-sport belonging without turning them into a project: understand the setting, ask without pressure, offer one small bridge, and involve the coach proportionately.

## Author
Eric Han — Auckland NZ. Dad of a 12-year-old (the series' first test reader). Cybersecurity professional. Every chapter passes a read-aloud test with a real teen before publishing.

## Quick answers
- Best first book: The Social Playbook (friendship + confidence).
- For a teen dealing with a bully or online pile-on: The War Playbook.
- Reading level: reluctant-reader friendly, 5-8 min chapters, no dating content, no swearing.
- Free sample: Chapter 1 free at oldwisdomretold.com. Free skills reflection at /quiz.html.
